articles.title: Build a free shipping progress bar for Shopify with Liquid and JavaScript
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I work on Brix, a Shopify cart app. This post shows how to build the feature yourself, and Brix is mentioned only at the end. A free shipping progress bar is one of the simplest cart featu…
articles.body: Disclosure: I work on Brix, a Shopify cart app. This post shows how to build the feature yourself, and Brix is mentioned only at the end. A free shipping progress bar is one of the simplest cart features to add, and it works because it makes a goal visible: "You're $12 away from free shipping." In this post we will build one with a Liquid snippet, a little CSS and a short script that keeps it in step with the cart. It is written for a standard Online Store 2.0 theme such as Dawn. Themes differ, so treat the code as a starting point and test it in your own theme. What we are building A bar that fills as the cart total approaches a threshold. A message that says how much more to spend, then switches to a success message.

articles.title: APA vs. MLA vs. Chicago: A Developer's Guide to Citation Formats (and a Tiny Formatter in TypeScript)
articles.excerpt: Citation formatting is a strange corner of academic life. The rules are precise, they differ from style to style, and they change between editions. Students lose points for a misplaced period or a mis…
articles.body: Citation formatting is a strange corner of academic life. The rules are precise, they differ from style to style, and they change between editions. Students lose points for a misplaced period or a missing italic, and the frustration is real because the rules feel arbitrary. To a developer, though, a citation looks very familiar. It's structured data (author, title, year, publisher, URL) rendered through a template. Different styles are just different templates operating on the same fields. Once you see it that way, the whole thing becomes a lot less mysterious, and you can reason about it the same way you'd reason about a serializer.
articles.author: Alan Matthew

articles.title: Building a Secrets Detection Pre-Commit Hook in 50 Lines
articles.excerpt: Secrets leaking into git repositories cause a disproportionate share of real-world breaches. AWS keys committed to a public GitHub repo get scraped by bots within minutes — sometimes seconds. The fix…
articles.body: Secrets leaking into git repositories cause a disproportionate share of real-world breaches. AWS keys committed to a public GitHub repo get scraped by bots within minutes — sometimes seconds. The fix is to catch them before they ever reach the commit, not after. Why a pre-commit hook? CI/CD scanners catch leaks after the fact. The commit is already in history at that point, and you need to rotate the secret, scrub the history with git filter-branch or BFG, and hope no bot grabbed it in the window between push and detection. A pre-commit hook runs locally before the commit lands — zero-latency interception. There are heavy tools like truffleHog , gitleaks , and detect-secrets . They're excellent for large organizations.
articles.author: Ayi NEDJIMI

articles.title: A Model Registry With an Outbound Dial: What CVE-2026-64849 Hands an Unauthenticated Caller
articles.excerpt: A Model Registry With an Outbound Dial: What CVE-2026-64849 Hands an Unauthenticated Caller MLflow accumulates privilege quietly. Experiment tracking, artefact storage and the model registry sit behin…
articles.body: A Model Registry With an Outbound Dial: What CVE-2026-64849 Hands an Unauthenticated Caller MLflow accumulates privilege quietly. Experiment tracking, artefact storage and the model registry sit behind one HTTP service, and that service is normally reachable from the same segment as the object store, the internal package index and whatever metadata endpoint the cloud provider exposes. So a webhook handler that fetches a caller-supplied URL without checking who is calling is not really a webhook problem. It is a question about everything the server can reach. What the flaw actually is CVE-2026-64849 covers a missing authentication check on the MLflow webhook endpoint.

articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built Why don't I clean it? Because of the Hoarder’s Paradox: I am way too lazy to sort nearly a thou…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built Let’s be honest about the Downloads folder. For most developers and students, it is a digital graveyard. Mine had accumulated exactly 962 files—a chaotic mix of university PDFs, C# snippets, .jar game mods, audio tracks, and 40 different setup_v2_final(1).exe installers. Why don't I clean it? Because of the Hoarder’s Paradox: I am way too lazy to sort nearly a thousand files manually. I am too paranoid to bulk-delete anything because "what if I need that random file from 4 months ago?!" To channel my inner sloth for International Sloth Day, I built Sloth AI Folder Tidier—an automated file organizer designed specifically for lazy digital hoarders.

articles.title: System Design of a Synthetic Consciousness: Architecting a Biological Brain from Scratch in Python (Zero Commercial LLMs)
articles.excerpt: _We like to believe we are something special. It comforts us to think that our choices spring from an ineffable spark called "consciousness," or from a sacred liberty we name "free will." But look clo…
articles.body: _We like to believe we are something special. It comforts us to think that our choices spring from an ineffable spark called "consciousness," or from a sacred liberty we name "free will." But look closely, and there is no ghost in the machine. A living organism is nothing more than a broth of stochastic chemical reactions, nudged by ambient thermodynamics and colliding against other chemical reactions. The molecules firing inside your synapses do not know they are thinking; the neurotransmitters dictating your panic or your euphoria have no concept of who you are. And it is precisely there—in that absolute ignorance of our own internal machinery—where the illusion is born.
articles.author: David San Nicolás Montero

That is the size of the internal buffer the Brotli decoder inside Node.js kept writing past, according to the Node.js security advisory of October 21 . Feed it the wrong compressed stream and, in the advisory's words, an attacker "can corrupt process memory, which can lead to a crash, disclosure of process memory, or remote code execution." articles.body: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history.  Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano aboard the Orion spacecraft into low Earth orbit to perform a series of demonstrations with test versions, or test articles, of human landing systems being developed by industry partners Blue Origin and SpaceX. During the planned 14-day mission, crews and flight controllers will practice the rendezvous, docking, habitation, and operational procedures that will be essential when Artemis astronauts begin landing near the Moon’s South Pole in 2028.
